entities.summary:
The Battle of the Ice, fought on April 12, 1242, near Lake Peipus in Eastern Europe, was a pivotal event in the Northern Crusades. This battle saw a combined force of Novgorod and Swedish warriors clash with the Livonian Crusader army, resulting in a decisive victory for the pagans and a significant setback for the Christian knights.

The Battle of the Ice was a crucial turning point in the Northern Crusades, as it halted the Christian advance into Eastern Europe and allowed the pagan states of Novgorod and Pskov to consolidate their power.

The legacy of the Battle of the Ice can be seen in the continued resistance of the pagan states against the Christian crusaders, which ultimately led to the signing of the Treaty of Nöteborg in 1323, recognizing the border between Sweden and Novgorod.

As stated by the chronicler of the Novgorod First Chronicle, 'the Lord granted us a great victory over the Christians', highlighting the enduring impact of this battle on the spiritual and cultural landscape of Eastern Europe.

The Battle of the Ice also showed the strategic importance of the region around Lake Peipus, which would continue to be a focal point of power struggles between the Christian and pagan states for centuries to come.
